title: India Becomes World's Top 'Brain Centre' for Retail & FMCG Giants
description: India is now the leading global hub for "Global Capability Centres" (GCCs) in retail and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sectors. These centres are like adv.

faq.a: GCC stands for Global Capability Centre.

faq.q: Which global companies have these retail and FMCG GCCs in India?
faq.a: Many leading global brands, including Walmart Global Tech, Tesco, Target, H&M, Lowe's, L'Oréal, and AB InBev, have set up their GCCs in India.

faq.q: What kind of jobs are typically created in these centres?
faq.a: Jobs range from AI specialists, data scientists, and product engineers to cybersecurity experts, cloud computing professionals, and roles in research and development.

faq.q: How much is this sector expected to grow in India?
faq.a: The GCC ecosystem is projected to generate $98.4 billion in revenue by the end of FY2026 and could grow to between $155 billion and $199 billion by FY2030.

faq.q: Is AI playing a big role in India's GCC growth?
faq.a: Yes, India leads all major GCC markets in AI adoption, with 5-7% of the retail GCC workforce already in AI-related roles.
